decision: harness lives in a new apps/perf workspace, not loose files in scripts/
why: a workspace gets typecheck, knip and tests through turbo, keeps lighthouse and puppeteer dev-only and scoped, and can import eval and sdk sources the way apps/e2e does

decision: seed through the real runner API instead of raw SQL inserts
why: rows then match what production writes, and the seeder keeps working when the eval tables change

decision: count DB queries with a bun preload that wraps pg Client.query in the server process
why: local Postgres has no pg_stat_statements preloaded and restarting the shared cluster is off limits; the preload counts exactly without touching server code

decision: seed 6 suites x 10 cases x 3 variants x 3 trials, 3 batches each, instead of 25 cases
why: a batch may hold at most 100 trials and an org 3 open batches; the first plan was refused by runner.start

decision: fail the whole run when any measured request errors
why: a broken endpoint answering fast 4xx would otherwise read as a speedup

decision: fake the OpenAI judge by wrapping fetch in the bench process, and skip simulated users
why: no live model runs are budgeted; the command harness cannot resume, so a simulated user cannot take a turn on it

decision: per step timings come from the eval code's own Effect spans through a recording tracer
why: no instrumentation added to the runner, and the steps stay named as the code names them

decision: Lighthouse default mobile throttling with a cleared cache, not the desktop preset
why: desktop scored every page 100 with 0 ms TBT, which cannot show a regression; mobile gave 55 to 56 with real spread
evidence: quick web runs before and after the switch

decision: '--target and ab run a second checkout's server, web and runner from this harness
why: owners need main versus branch today, before this harness is on main

decision: replaced process level A B A B with in process paired lanes: both checkouts booted at once, alternating blocks per endpoint, trial and page
why: main against main as two separate full runs showed 54 regressions and 51 improvements at 5%, all latency, from other agents loading the machine

decision: a regression must also land past the before side's worst round; seed time, memory after seed and web build time are informational
why: A/A runs moved those by 10 to 16 percent with no code change

decision: one browser context per checkout
why: a paired A/A showed the second lane's trial page rendering 164 DOM nodes: the first server's session cookies leaked across ports on 127.0.0.1
result: quick paired run shows equal DOM nodes 13842 both lanes

decision: the heap reading fails unless the trial page shows a seeded journal command
why: the cookie bug above produced a plausible looking 72 percent heap improvement
